questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

Hardly had he come out of the (1)/ cinema hall then the bomb exploded (2)/ and shattered the hall completely. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'Hardly' and 'when' are **correlative conjunctions**.
 
• **Correlative conjunctions** are sort of like tag-team conjunctions. They come in **pairs**, and you have to use both of them in different places in a sentence to make them work. They get their name from the fact that they work together (co-) and relate one sentence element to another.
 
 
• For example: **Hardly** had I reached the station **when **the train left.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, as 'Hardly' is present in part (1) of the sentence, the correlative conjunction that must be used in (2) should be 'when'.
 
• Hence, 'then' should be replaced by 'when' to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Hardly had he come out of the cinema hall** when** the bomb exploded and shattered the hall completely.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Some of the important Correlative Conjunctions are:
 
 
• Either….or
 
• Neither….nor
 
• **Hardly….when**
 
• Scarcely….when
 
• Both…and
 
• If…then
 
• Not only….but also
 
• Rather….than
 
• Whether…or
 
• No sooner…than
 
• Else…but
 
• Lest…should
 
• Other…than
 
• So…that
